verdict.rationale: CodeRabbit documents context-aware reviews. It applies existing repository guideline files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursorrules) as review criteria, and it detects breaking changes and API mismatches across linked repositories, so reviews reach beyond the changed hunks for conventions and cross-repo dependencies. However, no evidence shows that a standard PR review analyzes in-repo call sites or related modules of changed code; AI Deep Scan's beyond-the-diff analysis covers only security issues and is separately metered. Missing for 10: documented in-repo call-site/related-module analysis during PR review, evidence of convention inference beyond explicit guideline files, independent hands-on corroboration of repository-wide context.

support.subject: As a developer, review comments reflect the whole repository — call sites, related modules, existing conventions — not just the changed hunks

citations.quote: CodeRabbit automatically detects coding guideline files such as .cursorrules, CLAUDE.md, and AGENTS.md in your repository and applies them as review criteria
Link related repositories so CodeRabbit can detect breaking changes, API mismatches, and dependency issues that cross repository boundaries during code review.
analyzes committed source code and infrastructure configuration for exploitable vulnerabilities and exposed secrets beyond the current pull request diff
